National Outdoor Recreation Conference 2025
The National Outdoor Recreation Conference 2025 was held on 26th 
June at the Radisson Blu Hotel in Limerick and attended by staff 
from the Rural and Community Development Directorate. Hosted 
by the Department of Rural and Community Development (DRCDG) 
and Comhairle na Tuaithe, the conference focused on “Embracing 
Ireland’s Outdoors - Working together to deliver high quality 
and sustainable outdoor recreation opportunities.” The annual 
conference aims to bring together the key national stakeholders 
in outdoor recreation to provide networking opportunities, share 
best practice and inform policy implementation and future policy 
development. It included a session on responsible behaviour in the 
outdoors and also heard contributions from some of the trailblazing 
organisations in the sector.
The event was highly relevant to local authorities, particularly in 
the context of the development, delivery, and funding of outdoor 
recreation projects through national programmes such as ORIS 
(Outdoor Recreation Infrastructure Scheme).
Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht, 
Dara Calleary TD, addressed the conference and launched the 
‘Recreation in Ireland’s Outdoors’ booklet. The booklet has been 
developed for landowners who provide recreational access to their 
lands, and recreational users, and informs them of their rights and 
obligations. Attendees also had the opportunity to participate in 
local outdoor activities, including a visit to the Limerick Greenway.

Mens Health Event 2025
On Thursday 12th June, Clare County 
Council, Healthy Clare and Ennis Medical 
Center, came together to host a Mens 
Health Day event in the Buttermarket. 
With over 90 men in attendance, the 
event which was delivered to council staff 
and the wider community showcased 
supports and resources available to 
support men covering a range of topics 
to include; lifestyle medicine, cancer 
awareness 
and 
prevention, 
sleep 
hygience, positive mental health, phyiscal activity and health literacy. 
Speaking at the event Ann Reynolds, Director of Service Rural 
Department, stated that ‘Cultural norms, societal pressures, and 
simple lack of awareness have led to many men ignoring symptoms, 
delaying check-ups, and missing opportunities for early intervention. 
Today, we stand together, shoulder to shoulder to change that trend 
here in Co. Clare, as we look to ensure that we all understand the 
importance of prioritising our physical and mental well-being’.
Feedback on the event has been positive, showing a clear need to 
continue raising awareness throughout the county on mens health 
and wellbeing. 
Other stakeholers who came together in the delivery of the event 
included; HSE, Mental Health Ireland, Clare Sports Partnership, the 
National Office of Suicide Prevention, LCETB, SOLAS, Employability 
Clare, GROW, FASD.

Clare Garden Festival: Extending the Season 
(Insert Image 4: Ennis Mens Shed Extending the Season Event )
22 individuals attended a planting workshop at Ennis Mens Shed 
on 19th June. Showcasing the new polytunnel which was secured 
through a climate grant. The members of Ennis Mens Shed 
encouraged participants to stroll around the facility to see how they 
have managed to grow produce outside of the traditional growing 
season. The main speaker at the event, Rebecca Cronin, gave a 
workshop on the Healthy Clare theme of ‘Extending the Season’ 
supporitng individuals to plant in small containers that can be used 
to develop food from the garden. This day was also supported 
by Clare Local Development Company, who are working with 
community gardens across Co. Clare assessing support needs. Of the 
22 individual who attended the event, all said that they left with skills 
and knowledge to continue growing at home.

Healthy Clare Micro Fund 2025
On Thursday 26th of June, O’Currys GAA, with support from the 
Healthy Clare Micro Fund, delivered an inspiring talk by Dessie 
Fitzgeard on the importance of resililience in times of stress and 
the tools that he has used to become more resillient. Such tools 
have included; taking responsibility and making choices, identifying 
personal strength than can be found in vulnerability, goal setting and 
practicing gratitude. 
The evening was aimed at promoting mental well-being through 
engaging activities and motivational talks. By creating a supportive 
environment, the committee hope to reduce stigma around mental 
health and encourage open discussions. This event and subsequent 
events will foster connections, promote resilience, and empower 
participants to prioritise their mental health, ultimately contributing 
to a healthier community. 
BOI Event 
Clare Age Friendly was honoured to participate as a guest speaker at 
the recent Bank of Ireland "Protecting Your Home, Protecting Your 
Finances" event, held on May 28th at 10:30 AM in the Old Ground 
Hotel.
The panel featured esteemed speakers, including Grace Murphy 
from the Bank of Ireland Fraud Department, Sharon Cahir of Cahir 
Solicitors, and Ann Marie Walshe, Senior Advice Consultant at Bank 
of Ireland.
The primary objective of the event was to provide valuable insights 
into fraud prevention, Enduring Power of Attorney, and safeguarding 
personal finances for the future. The event was well-attended and 
received highly positive feedback from participants.
Return of the Cultural Companions 
The Clare Age Friendly Programme, in collaboration with Creative 
Ireland, was thrilled to warmly welcome back members of the Clare 
Cultural Companions for a special gathering on May 29th at Glór.
The event was filled with lively conversations, reconnecting 
friendships, and a warm atmosphere. Attendees were greeted with 
refreshments and a chance to catch up before enjoying a screening 
of Housewife of the Year, which sparked plenty of discussion and 
nostalgia.
It was truly a heartwarming occasion, celebrating the vibrancy of 
Clare’s cultural community and the joy of shared experiences. Here's 
to many more inspiring get-togethers ahead!

The event was attended by Clare’s Age Friendly Ambassador, Mike 
Hanrahan; Chairperson of the Clare Older People’s Council, Mary 
O’Callaghan; and Clare Age Friendly Programme Manager, Shanelle 
Waring. All Age Friendly Ambassadors were invited, and their 
voluntary work was warmly acknowledged and commended.

a toolkit designed to scale up creative initiatives that support the 
wellbeing of older people.

Pedestrianisation Trial for Killaloe Bridge
Following engagement with a range of stakeholders by officials 
from Clare and Tipperary County Councils, in February of this year 
both local authorities agreed to pedestrianise the existing Killaloe 
Bridge for a trial period.
In June following a meeting between Elected Members of Killaloe 
and Nenagh Municipal Districts and officials from Clare and 
Tipperary County Councils the trial pedestrianisation of the old 
bridge linking Killaloe and Ballina will run from Monday, 28 July 
2025 to Friday, 17 October 2025.
 
The trial, provided for under Section 38 of the Road Traffic Act 
1994, aims to pilot a more pedestrian and cyclist-friendly route on 
the existing bridge between Killaloe and Ballina. The trial will also 
enable further detail and evidence of traffic flows and pedestrian 
movements between the towns to be gathered, and for the social, 
economic and tourism benefits to be measured.
Following completion of the trial period, and having regard to the 
submissions made, consideration of national, regional and local 
policy and an appraisal of all data gathered, both Tipperary County 
Council and Clare County Council will make a determination on the 
future arrangements and pedestrianisation of the old 18th Century 
bridge.

LOCAL AUTHORITY INTEGRATION TEAM
The Local Authority Integration Teams (LAITs) have been set up 
in all local authorities. Their purpose is to help coordinate the 
different kinds of support available for people who are applying 
for international protection, refugees, and others in similar 
situations. 
The goal of LAITs is to help IP applicants and refugees become 
independent, settle into their new communities, and participate 
in Irish life. They do this by connecting people to important 
services that can help them integrate into the community. 
Who do LAITs support? 
LAITs provide support for: 
•	
Applicants for International Protection (IP) 
•	
People who have been granted refugee status or other 
forms of protection, such as subsidiary protection or 
permission to remain 
•	
Refugees who have been resettled in Ireland through a 
government programme 
•	
Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection (BOTPs) 
 
How is the support provided? 
LAITs operate under the principle of 'Integration from Day One'. 
This means that LAITs provide integration support to people 
who need it as soon as they arrive in Ireland. 
What services do LAITs provide? 
The work of LAITs isn’t meant to replace existing services. 
Instead, LAITs help connect people with the existing services 
that are most suitable for their needs. This includes things like: 
•	
Being a direct contact for new arrivals, helping them with 
any problems they might have when dealing with public 
services 
•	
Connecting new arrivals with services like legal help, 
childcare and healthcare 
•	
Connecting new arrivals with services that improve their 
ability to live independently, like job training, English 
classes, education, and apprenticeships 
•	
Guiding new arrivals through the process of applying for 
financial support, medical help, child benefits, and other 
services they might need 
•	
Holding meetings in local areas and using community 
development principles to help those who attend 
•	
Supporting people if they face racism or other unfair 
treatment, helping them report it to the right authorities 
•	
Helping vulnerable new arrivals get in touch with non-
governmental organisations (NGOs) and other services if 
they need extra help 
 
How do I contact my Local Authority Integration Team? 
You can contact LAIT's by email on integration@clarecoco.ie

Strategic Integrated Framework Plan (SIFP) for the Shannon Estuary
The SIFP Steering Group held a meeting on the 10th of June in the 
offices of Clare County Council where the review of the National 
Development Plan was discussed in terms of the importance 
of aligning capital investment under the NDP with national, 
regional and local policy objectives and recognising the essen-
tial enabling function that Shannon Foynes Port Company, ESB 
Moneypoint and others operating within the Shannon Estuary 
have in delivering on the Renewable Energy sector and in par-
ticular the Offshore Floating Wind sector. Clare County Council 
as lead authority, are currently preparing a submission to the 
NDP review on behalf of the Steering Group members which 
will focus on the funding and infrastructure required to deliver 
on this critical sector within the Shannon Estuary. 
Dr Ross O’Connell of MaREI (Centre for Marine and Renewable 
Energy) presented on the National Wet Storage Study for float-
ing wind, which was a MaREI, ESB and SFPC collaboration. The 
presentation outlined how for large scale FLOW projects, it is 
anticipated that Wind Turbines and their associated sub-struc-
ture will need to be temporarily stored in port until deployment 
becomes possible during an appropriate weather window. 
Due to the harsh wave climate off Ireland’s west coast, it will 
lead to a narrow weather window for FLOW installation. The 
study identified that there are potential areas at different depth 
thresholds where wet storage sites could potentially be located. 
Further studies will be necessary to establish this at a site spe-
cific level.
